name: ai-news
description: Answer "what's new in AI" questions from dated AI news briefings, citing the source posts
readme:
Read it · Browse 41 categories · Plug it into your agent · Search the archive
Checked against the source
A number, unit, model version or name that is not in the source post gets the briefing rejected and rewritten.		 Every claim has a link
The original post and the page it points to, copied by code, never written by the model.		 41 categories
Models, dev tools, research and funding, plus robotics, climate, quantum, security and crypto.		 Ready for your agent
MCP server, Agent Skill, JSON API and llms.txt. Plain Markdown under CC BY 4.0.
## Three ways in

Read it

The newest digests on blogs.drix10.com, with search, topic pages and an RSS feed. Or open any category below and read its latest digest here on GitHub.

Star and watch the repo to get new digests as they land.

Ask it from your agent

Claude, Cursor, VS Code or Windsurf answer "what did Anthropic ship this week?" from the briefings, with dates and source links. No key, no account. Setup for every client ↓

claude mcp add ai-resources -- npx -y ai-resources-mcp

Clone it

100,000+ dated, sourced briefings in plain Markdown for RAG, evals or an offline index. Every resources-NNN.md holds 5 to 12 of them, like this one.

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Drix10/ai-resources
## What a briefing looks like

A real briefing from AI Developer Tools #296. Every digest file holds 5 to 12 of these.

## Signals: what is accelerating in AI

Signals, computed weekly: topics whose coverage climbs three weeks running. Trajectories, not predictions — and nothing on it is written by a model.

Briefings tell you what happened. Signals tells you what it means: which topics are accelerating, with the sample headlines and source links behind every call. Computed from counts only (one briefing = one vote), in the open: [`MOVEMENTS.md`](MOVEMENTS.md) in this repo, [`/api/signals`](https://blogs.drix10.com/api/signals) for code, and the `trending_movements` MCP tool for agents. ## Who it is for - **Engineers building with AI.** What changed in models, inference, agents, MCP and dev tools, with the benchmark number and the link, in [AI Developer Tools](#ai-developer-tools) and [Tech Infrastructure](#tech-infrastructure). - **Founders and investors.** Rounds, launches and revenue figures as they are announced, in [AI Companies and Ventures](#ai-companies-and-ventures), [VC Firms](#vc-firms) and [Founders and Entrepreneurs](#founders-and-entrepreneurs). - **Researchers and students.** What the people in the field are publishing and arguing about, in [CS Academics](#cs-academics) and [Neuroscience and AI](#neuroscience-and-ai). - **Anyone building RAG, agents or evals.** A 100,000-item corpus of dated, sourced AI news under CC BY 4.0. Awesome lists are still the better pick for a vetted shortlist, and a newsletter for five editor-picked minutes a day. [COMPARISONS.md](COMPARISONS.md) lays out where this fits. ## Use it from your AI agent Five ways to plug the briefings into an agent or your own code. None needs a key or an account. Full reference: **[USE-WITH-AI.md](USE-WITH-AI.md)**. | Path | Best for | Setup | | --- | --- | --- | | [MCP server](#mcp-server) | Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf | one command or one JSON block | | [Agent Skill](#agent-skill) | Claude Code and other Skill-aware agents | copy one folder | | [JSON API](#json-api) | your own code, custom GPT actions, scripts | none, CORS open | | [llms.txt and RSS](#llmstxt-and-rss) | any LLM that reads a URL, feed readers, bots | none | | [Raw Markdown](#three-ways-in) | RAG, evals, offline indexes, all 100,000+ briefings | `git clone` | ### MCP server Published on npm as [`ai-resources-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ai-resources-mcp) (MIT, code in [`mcp/`](mcp/)). `npx` fetches it on first run, so there is nothing to install by hand. | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `search_briefings(query, category?, limit?, since?)` | Keyword search, newest first. All words must match. `since` is `YYYY-MM-DD`. | | `latest(category?, limit?)` | The newest briefings, overall or for one category. | | `get_briefing(id)` | Full Markdown of one briefing (URL or slug), with every source link. | | `list_categories()` | Every category slug with its briefing count. | | `trending_movements(limit?)` | Topics accelerating week over week (rising) or hot for one week (watch), with sample headlines and source links. | Every result ends with its source link and `Data: github.com/Drix10/ai-resources (CC BY 4.0)`, so answers stay citable. **Claude Code** ```bash claude mcp add ai-resources -- npx -y ai-resources-mcp ```
Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf
Add this to `claude_desktop_config.json` (Claude Desktop: Settings → Developer → Edit Config), `~/.cursor/mcp.json` or `.cursor/mcp.json` (Cursor), or `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` (Windsurf): ```json { "mcpServers": { "ai-resources": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "ai-resources-mcp"] } } } ```
VS Code
In `.vscode/mcp.json`, or *MCP: Open User Configuration*: ```json { "servers": { "ai-resources": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "ai-resources-mcp"] } } } ``` Or from a terminal: ```bash code --add-mcp "{\"name\":\"ai-resources\",\"command\":\"npx\",\"args\":[\"-y\",\"ai-resources-mcp\"]}" ```
Windows, and other settings
If a client cannot start `npx` on Windows, use `"command": "cmd", "args": ["/c", "npx", "-y", "ai-resources-mcp"]`. `AI_RESOURCES_API_URL` sets the API base URL (default `https://blogs.drix10.com`).
Then ask, for example: - *"What did Anthropic announce this week? Cite the sources."* - *"Latest five briefings in AI Developer Tools."* - *"Who raised a Series A in AI this month, and how much?"* ### Agent Skill [`skills/ai-news`](skills/ai-news/SKILL.md) teaches an agent when and how to answer "what's new in AI", "latest on <model or company>" and "who raised" questions from the briefings, with dates and citations. It uses the MCP tools when they are installed and falls back to the JSON API, then llms.txt, then raw Markdown on GitHub when they are not. ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Drix10/ai-resources mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills cp -r ai-resources/skills/ai-news ~/.claude/skills/ ```
One project only, Windows, other agents
- **One project:** copy it to `.claude/skills/ai-news/` inside that project instead. - **Windows (PowerShell):** `Copy-Item -Recurse ai-resources\skills\ai-news $HOME\.claude\skills\` - **Other agents** that read `SKILL.md` folders work the same way. For chat apps without Skills, paste the body of `SKILL.md` into the custom instructions.
### JSON API Base URL `https://blogs.drix10.com`. JSON, CORS open, no key. It covers the briefings published on the blog; the full archive is in this repository. | Request | Returns | | --- | --- | | `GET /api/articles?q=&category=&since=&limit=&page=` | `{ items, total, page, limit, totalPages, license }`, newest first. All words in `q` must match; every parameter is optional. | | `GET /api/articles?slug=` | One item, plus `content` (the full Markdown). | | `GET /api/categories` | `{ items: [{ name, slug, count, url, llms }] }` | Each item has `title`, `url`, `slug`, `category`, `categorySlug`, `date`, `description`, `headlines` (every news item in the briefing) and `sources` (`[{ title, url }]`, the original posts). ```bash curl "https://blogs.drix10.com/api/articles?q=anthropic&since=2026-10-01&limit=5" curl "https://blogs.drix10.com/api/categories" ``` ### llms.txt and RSS - [`/llms.txt`](https://blogs.drix10.com/llms.txt): the index, linking every category. - `/llms/.txt`: the 50 newest briefings of one category, for example [`/llms/ai-developer-tools.txt`](https://blogs.drix10.com/llms/ai-developer-tools.txt). - [`/rss.xml`](https://blogs.drix10.com/rss.xml): for feed readers, Slack or Discord feed bots and email-digest services. When you show the data anywhere, credit it as `Data: github.com/Drix10/ai-resources (CC BY 4.0)`. The MCP server and the Skill add that line for you. ## By the numbers Counted from this repository on 29 October 2026. The archive only grows. | | | | ---: | --- | | **100,000+** | briefings: a headline, two or three sentences and the key numbers, one per post | | **10,800+** | digest files (`resources-NNN.md`) across **41 categories** | | **10,900+** | commits since November 2024, all made by an automated pipeline | | **14,000+** | briefings that link both the original post and the page it points to (every briefing since mid-2026) | | **~2,000** | of them published as articles on [blogs.drix10.com](https://blogs.drix10.com) with search, topic pages, an [RSS feed](https://blogs.drix10.com/rss.xml) and [llms.txt](https://blogs.drix10.com/llms.txt) | ## How it is built Nobody types these. A pipeline reads the hand-picked X lists for each category, writes one briefing per strong post, runs the fact gates, strips secrets, de-duplicates across categories and commits the batch here. The same run refreshes the category list below and publishes to the blog. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Hand-picked X lists (41 categories)"] --> B["One briefing per post"] B --> C["Fact gates: numbers, units, versions and names must be in the post; links copied by code"] C --> D["resources-NNN.md committed here"] D --> E["blogs.drix10.com: search, topic pages, RSS, llms.txt"] ``` **Known limits:** briefings are machine-written from public posts and can still be wrong; check the linked source before you rely on a number. Part of the older archive (2024 to mid-2026) predates source links. Coverage follows the hand-picked lists, blind spots included. Inclusion is not endorsement. ## Contribute A pipeline writes the briefings. People pick the sources and fix what it gets wrong. Ways in: - **Pick up a [good first issue](https://github.com/Drix10/ai-resources/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22)**: MCP server tools, Skill phrasings, guides, examples, translations. - **[Suggest a source](https://github.com/Drix10/ai-resources/issues/new?template=suggest-source.yml)** (an X account, list or site) or **[report a wrong fact](https://github.com/Drix10/ai-resources/issues/new?template=wrong-fact.yml)** with the briefing link. - **Ask, share what you built, or float an idea** in [Discussions](https://github.com/Drix10/ai-resources/discussions). [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the details, including what not to edit by hand. Content is CC BY 4.0; the MCP server code is MIT. If you use the archive in research, [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff) has the citation. ## Star history ## About the curator Built and maintained by **[Drishtant Ghosh (Drix10)](https://drix10.com)**, an AI systems engineer and 1x acquired founder (ReeF, acquired August 2024) based in Bengaluru. Signals: what is accelerating in AI

<a href="https://blogs.drix10.com/signals"><img src="assets/readme/signals.jpg" alt="Signals page: topics whose briefing coverage climbs week over week, each with sample headlines and source links, plus the counting method" width="100%"></a>

<p align="center"><sub><a href="https://blogs.drix10.com/signals">Signals</a>, computed weekly: topics whose coverage climbs three weeks running. Trajectories, not predictions — and nothing on it is written by a model.</sub></p>

Briefings tell you what happened. Signals tells you what it means: which topics are accelerating, with the sample headlines and source links behind every call. Computed from counts only (one briefing = one vote), in the open: [MOVEMENTS.md](MOVEMENTS.md) in this repo, /api/signals for code, and the trending_movements MCP tool for agents.

Who it is for

  • Engineers building with AI. What changed in models, inference, agents, MCP and dev tools, with the benchmark number and the link, in [AI Developer Tools](#ai-developer-tools) and [Tech Infrastructure](#tech-infrastructure).
  • Founders and investors. Rounds, launches and revenue figures as they are announced, in [AI Companies and Ventures](#ai-companies-and-ventures), [VC Firms](#vc-firms) and [Founders and Entrepreneurs](#founders-and-entrepreneurs).
  • Researchers and students. What the people in the field are publishing and arguing about, in [CS Academics](#cs-academics) and [Neuroscience and AI](#neuroscience-and-ai).
  • Anyone building RAG, agents or evals. A 100,000-item corpus of dated, sourced AI news under CC BY 4.0.

Awesome lists are still the better pick for a vetted shortlist, and a newsletter for five editor-picked minutes a day. [COMPARISONS.md](COMPARISONS.md) lays out where this fits.

Use it from your AI agent

Five ways to plug the briefings into an agent or your own code. None needs a key or an account. Full reference: [USE-WITH-AI.md](USE-WITH-AI.md).

| Path | Best for | Setup |

| --- | --- | --- |

| [MCP server](#mcp-server) | Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf | one command or one JSON block |

| [Agent Skill](#agent-skill) | Claude Code and other Skill-aware agents | copy one folder |

| [JSON API](#json-api) | your own code, custom GPT actions, scripts | none, CORS open |

| [llms.txt and RSS](#llmstxt-and-rss) | any LLM that reads a URL, feed readers, bots | none |

| [Raw Markdown](#three-ways-in) | RAG, evals, offline indexes, all 100,000+ briefings | git clone |

MCP server

<a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/ai-resources-mcp"><img src="https://img.shields.io/npm/v/ai-resources-mcp?style=flat-square&logo=npm&color=cb3837&label=ai-resources-mcp" alt="ai-resources-mcp on npm"></a>

<a href="https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=io.github.Drix10/ai-resources"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP%20Registry-io.github.Drix10%2Fai--resources-8b9cff?style=flat-square" alt="In the official MCP Registry"></a>

<img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D18-3ecf8e?style=flat-square&logo=node.js&logoColor=white" alt="Node.js 18 or newer">

Published on npm as ai-resources-mcp (MIT, code in [mcp/](mcp/)). npx fetches it on first run, so there is nothing to install by hand.

| Tool | What it does |

| --- | --- |

| search_briefings(query, category?, limit?, since?) | Keyword search, newest first. All words must match. since is YYYY-MM-DD. |

| latest(category?, limit?) | The newest briefings, overall or for one category. |

| get_briefing(id) | Full Markdown of one briefing (URL or slug), with every source link. |

| list_categories() | Every category slug with its briefing count. |

| trending_movements(limit?) | Topics accelerating week over week (rising) or hot for one week (watch), with sample headlines and source links. |

Every result ends with its source link and Data: github.com/Drix10/ai-resources (CC BY 4.0), so answers stay citable.

Claude Code


claude mcp add ai-resources -- npx -y ai-resources-mcp

<details>

<summary><b>Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf</b></summary>

<br>

Add this to claude_desktop_config.json (Claude Desktop: Settings → Developer → Edit Config), ~/.cursor/mcp.json or .cursor/mcp.json (Cursor), or ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json (Windsurf):


{

  "mcpServers": {

    "ai-resources": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "ai-resources-mcp"] }

  }

}

</details>

<details>

<summary><b>VS Code</b></summary>

<br>

In .vscode/mcp.json, or *MCP: Open User Configuration*:


{

  "servers": {

    "ai-resources": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "ai-resources-mcp"] }

  }

}

Or from a terminal:


code --add-mcp "{\"name\":\"ai-resources\",\"command\":\"npx\",\"args\":[\"-y\",\"ai-resources-mcp\"]}"

</details>

<details>

<summary><b>Windows, and other settings</b></summary>

<br>

If a client cannot start npx on Windows, use "command": "cmd", "args": ["/c", "npx", "-y", "ai-resources-mcp"].

AI_RESOURCES_API_URL sets the API base URL (default https://blogs.drix10.com).

</details>

Then ask, for example:

  • *"What did Anthropic announce this week? Cite the sources."*
  • *"Latest five briefings in AI Developer Tools."*
  • *"Who raised a Series A in AI this month, and how much?"*

Agent Skill

[skills/ai-news](skills/ai-news/SKILL.md) teaches an agent when and how to answer "what's new in AI", "latest on <model or company>" and "who raised" questions from the briefings, with dates and citations. It uses the MCP tools when they are installed and falls back to the JSON API, then llms.txt, then raw Markdown on GitHub when they are not.


git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Drix10/ai-resources

mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills

cp -r ai-resources/skills/ai-news ~/.claude/skills/

<details>

<summary><b>One project only, Windows, other agents</b></summary>

<br>

  • One project: copy it to .claude/skills/ai-news/ inside that project instead.
  • Windows (PowerShell): Copy-Item -Recurse ai-resources\skills\ai-news $HOME\.claude\skills\
  • Other agents that read SKILL.md folders work the same way. For chat apps without Skills, paste the body of SKILL.md into the custom instructions.

</details>

JSON API

Base URL https://blogs.drix10.com. JSON, CORS open, no key. It covers the briefings published on the blog; the full archive is in this repository.

| Request | Returns |

| --- | --- |

| GET /api/articles?q=&category=&since=&limit=&page= | { items, total, page, limit, totalPages, license }, newest first. All words in q must match; every parameter is optional. |

| GET /api/articles?slug=<slug or URL> | One item, plus content (the full Markdown). |

| GET /api/categories | { items: [{ name, slug, count, url, llms }] } |

Each item has title, url, slug, category, categorySlug, date, description, headlines (every news item in the briefing) and sources ([{ title, url }], the original posts).


curl "https://blogs.drix10.com/api/articles?q=anthropic&since=2026-10-01&limit=5"

curl "https://blogs.drix10.com/api/categories"

llms.txt and RSS

  • /llms.txt: the index, linking every category.
  • /llms/<category-slug>.txt: the 50 newest briefings of one category, for example /llms/ai-developer-tools.txt.
  • /rss.xml: for feed readers, Slack or Discord feed bots and email-digest services.

When you show the data anywhere, credit it as Data: github.com/Drix10/ai-resources (CC BY 4.0). The MCP server and the Skill add that line for you.

By the numbers

Counted from this repository on 29 October 2026. The archive only grows.

| | |

| ---: | --- |

| 100,000+ | briefings: a headline, two or three sentences and the key numbers, one per post |

| 10,800+ | digest files (resources-NNN.md) across 41 categories |

| 10,900+ | commits since November 2024, all made by an automated pipeline |

| 14,000+ | briefings that link both the original post and the page it points to (every briefing since mid-2026) |

| ~2,000 | of them published as articles on blogs.drix10.com with search, topic pages, an RSS feed and llms.txt |

How it is built

Nobody types these. A pipeline reads the hand-picked X lists for each category, writes one briefing per strong post, runs the fact gates, strips secrets, de-duplicates across categories and commits the batch here. The same run refreshes the category list below and publishes to the blog.


flowchart LR

    A["Hand-picked X lists (41 categories)"] --> B["One briefing per post"]

    B --> C["Fact gates: numbers, units, versions and names must be in the post; links copied by code"]

    C --> D["resources-NNN.md committed here"]

    D --> E["blogs.drix10.com: search, topic pages, RSS, llms.txt"]

Known limits: briefings are machine-written from public posts and can still be wrong; check the linked source before you rely on a number. Part of the older archive (2024 to mid-2026) predates source links. Coverage follows the hand-picked lists, blind spots included. Inclusion is not endorsement.

Contribute

A pipeline writes the briefings. People pick the sources and fix what it gets wrong. Ways in:

  • Pick up a good first issue: MCP server tools, Skill phrasings, guides, examples, translations.
  • Suggest a source (an X account, list or site) or report a wrong fact with the briefing link.
  • Ask, share what you built, or float an idea in Discussions.

[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the details, including what not to edit by hand. Content is CC BY 4.0; the MCP server code is MIT. If you use the archive in research, [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff) has the citation.

# AI news from the AI Resources briefings

The AI Resources knowledge base publishes daily briefings on AI models, companies, funding, tools and research. Each briefing groups several news items, each with key points and links to the original posts.

## Pick the access path

1. **MCP server installed** (tools named `search_briefings`, `latest`, `get_briefing`, `list_categories`, `trending_movements`): use those tools and skip the rest of this section.
   - For "what is trending / heating up in AI" questions, use `trending_movements` (rising or one-hot-week topics with sample headlines and sources).
   - If the installed server predates v1.1.0 and has no `trending_movements` tool, use `/api/signals` below for trending questions instead of skipping them.
2. **Otherwise use web fetch on the JSON API** (no key, CORS open):
   - Search: `https://blogs.drix10.com/api/articles?q=<words>&limit=10`
     - all words must match; keep queries to 1-3 distinctive words (`anthropic`, `series a`, `gemini`)
     - optional: `category=<slug>`, `since=YYYY-MM-DD`, `page=N`
   - Latest: `https://blogs.drix10.com/api/articles?limit=10` (add `category=<slug>` for one topic)
   - One briefing in full Markdown: `https://blogs.drix10.com/api/articles?slug=<slug or briefing URL>` (the item's `content`)
   - Categories and slugs: `https://blogs.drix10.com/api/categories`
   - Accelerating topics: `https://blogs.drix10.com/api/signals` — topics whose coverage climbs week over week, with sample headlines and links. Use it for "trending" questions; add `?category=<slug>` for one topic and `?limit=<n>` to see past the default first 10.
   - Each list item has `title`, `url`, `date`, `category`, `description`, `headlines` (every item in the briefing) and `sources` (`{title, url}`).
3. **Plain text instead of JSON**: `https://blogs.drix10.com/llms/<category-slug>.txt` lists a category's 50 newest briefings; `https://blogs.drix10.com/llms.txt` links them all.
4. **API down**: read raw Markdown on GitHub, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Drix10/ai-resources/main/<Category Name>/resources-<N>.md` (category folder names with spaces as `%20`; a higher N is newer). List a folder with `https://api.github.com/repos/Drix10/ai-resources/contents/<Category%20Name>`.

## How to answer

- For "latest"/"this week" questions, use `latest` or `since=` with a date about 7 days back. For "trending"/"heating up" questions, use `trending_movements` (or `/api/signals`, with `?category=` for one topic); report the stage (rising vs watch) and never present a watch item as confirmed. For a named model, company or person, search its name first, then a broader term if nothing matches.
- Search matches item titles and each briefing's opening text, so a match may sit in `headlines` rather than the title. Fetch the full briefing (`slug=`) before quoting details from it.
- Report what the briefings say with their dates. Do not fill gaps from memory; say when the briefings do not cover something.
- Cite every claim: link the briefing `url`, and the original post from `sources` when there is one.
- End the answer with: `Data: github.com/Drix10/ai-resources (CC BY 4.0)`.
